issues.legal_issue: A special procedure for evicting unauthorized occupants from public property is not invalid under the equality guarantee merely because authorities might apply it discriminatorily or because ordinary civil proceedings are also available.
material_facts: The challenged law provided a procedure intended to enable speedy eviction of unauthorized occupants from government premises.
The High Court allowed the constitutional writ petition solely on the ground that the law was unconstitutional, following an earlier High Court ruling.
The appeal challenged that decision, and the Supreme Court considered the law’s constitutionality under Article 14.
issues.conclusion: The law could not be treated as constitutionally infirm on the ground decided by the High Court. The Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court’s judgment, and remanded the matter for decision on the other grounds raised in the writ petition.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 14, a law providing a special procedure for speedy eviction of unauthorized occupants from public property is not invalid merely because it creates a possibility of discriminatory treatment or offers a procedure different from ordinary civil proceedings. A stated legislative purpose can provide sufficient guidance to authorities, and the procedure is not discriminatory merely because a special process is available; courts remain able to address discriminatory application. The Court applied Maganlal Chhagganlal (P) Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay, which disapproved the majority view in Northern India Caterers Private Ltd. v. State of Punjab, and followed State of Uttar Pradesh v. Arshad Ali Khan. It held that Raja Ram Verma v. State of Uttar Pradesh could no longer be treated as good law. Article 226 was the basis of the writ petition before the High Court.

rule.if: appeal_from_writ_judgment and special_process_for_unauthorized_public_occupants and special_process_aims_at_speedy_eviction and process_has_legislative_guidance and process_is_not_harsh_or_onerous and challenge_rests_on_possible_differential_treatment

predicates.appeal_from_writ_judgment: The matter is an appeal from a judgment on a constitutional writ petition.
predicates.special_process_for_unauthorized_public_: A law provides a special procedure for evicting unauthorized occupants from public property.
predicates.special_process_aims_at_speedy_eviction: The special procedure is intended to secure speedy eviction of unauthorized occupants.
predicates.process_has_legislative_guidance: The law’s stated purpose gives authorities guidance in deciding whether to use the special procedure.
predicates.process_is_not_harsh_or_onerous: The special procedure is not so harsh or onerous as to indicate discriminatory treatment.
predicates.challenge_rests_on_possible_differential: The challenge relies on the possibility that use of the special procedure could result in discriminatory treatment.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a writ judgment concerns a guided, non-harsh special process intended to speed eviction of unauthorized public-property occupants, and the challenge rests on possible discriminatory treatment, the special law is not invalid on that ground.
